title: Client cost vs fidelity tradeoffs (scratchbook)
text:
Purpose / context:
- quick personal scratchpad exploring levers we can expose or recommend for client-side request shaping to reduce server bill while preserving perceived output quality.
- aim: short list of heuristics + small experiments to try in client-side SDKs and proxy.
- audience: SDK + client-proxy owners, solutions eng for customer playbooks.

Open questions / constraints:
- acceptable user-perceived fidelity loss varies wildly by use-case (search vs code gen vs chat). need per-route presets.
- some levers change server compute (sampling, max_tokens) vs network (early streaming, chunking). quantify both.
- privacy: local truncation/censoring must preserve auditability for compliance customers.

Heuristics (draft):
1) adaptive max_tokens per intent
   - short: predict expected response length from prompt class and cap server-side max_tokens accordingly.
   - cheap predictor: n_chars_prompt -> buckets; or tiny local distilled model (10-50K params) to estimate tokens_out.
   - fallback: if server returns truncated=false and cost budget left, automatically request extension.

2) progressive fidelity stages (pipeline idea)
   - stage 0: deterministic constrained decode (greedy / low temp) quick sketch -> client displays partial response while server continues best-effort sampling for richer output.
   - stage 1: sampled decode (higher temp/top-p) for creative output, enabled only if route flagged as creative.
   - advantage: initial token latency low, client shows something, reduces wasted tokens when user accepts early.

3) streaming + early-accept heuristics
   - stream tokens to client; client heuristics to detect "good enough" (e.g., intent satisfied signals: contains slot X, code compiles, ends with signature).
   - if accept, send cancel request to server to stop generation -> saves tokens.
   - tricky: razor-fast cancel may still incur cost for tokens already generated on server; need backlog-aware cost estimate.

4) local lightweight post-filter / compression
   - run a small local quality filter (heuristic rules + cheap classifier) to decide whether to accept short answer or request full answer.
   - also compress/normalize repeated polymorphic content (e.g., answer lists) before sending upstream so server can spend tokens on content not formatting.

5) token-level sampling profiles exposed via SDK presets
   - presets: conservative (low temp, top_k 40), balanced (temp 0.7), creative (temp 1.0, top_p 0.95). map to cost multipliers and suggested max_tokens.

6) client caching of canonical answers & embeddings
   - for FAQ-like prompts, keep local small LRU of (normalized_prompt -> answer) + timestamp + verification checksum. If hit, serve locally. Invalidate by version id.

7) hybrid decode offload heuristic (edge-proxy)
   - allow edge-proxy to run a short decode (first 8-16 tokens) and estimate continuation entropy. If continuation entropy low -> ask server for concise finalization (low tokens). If entropy high -> route to richer model variant.

Metrics to capture (minimal set):
- tokens_saved_per_request (estimate)
- average server tokens per accepted_user_response
- fraction_of_early_accepts (client canceled after streaming)
- perceived_quality_drop (A/B, simple thumbs-up rate)
- added client CPU and p95 latency for prechecks

Simple cost model sketch (for local calc):
- server_cost = tokens_generated * unit_cost_model(route, model_variant)
- client_cost = client_cpu_ms * client_unit_cost + local_storage small
- net_saving = baseline_server_cost - server_cost - marginal_client_cost

Small ASCII flow (for notes):
  [Client] --(request + route_hint)--> [Edge proxy / SDK]
       |                                   |
       |-- local cache hit? --(serve)-->   |-- if miss -> route to hosted/dedicated cluster
       |                                   |       |
       |<-stream partial tokens--(cancel)->|       V
       |                                   |--> [Model cluster: staged decode -> sample -> finalize]--> store sample/cache

Experiment ideas (quick wins):
- A/B: streaming + early-accept + cancel vs baseline; measure tokens_saved_per_accept and NPS.
- Feature flag: per-route preset that reduces max_tokens by 30% to observe quality delta.
- Edge-proxy 8-token entropy probe: run on subsets of traffic and log correlation between initial entropy and final token count.

Risks / failure modes:
- user perceives lower quality: payback only if tokens_saved correlates with large % of traffic.
- cancel semantics differ across model backends; need consistent billing signals from infra (dedicated vs hosted).
- caching stale answers leads to correctness issues for dynamic data. store freshness TTL + version id.

Implementation notes / tasks:
- [ ] add per-route preset config in SDK with fields: preset_name, max_tokens_hint, sampling_profile, early_accept_rules_url, cache_ttl
- [ ] telemetry hooks: client should emit precheck_time_ms, cache_hit, early_accept_reason, cancel_latency_ms
- [ ] proposal PR: SDK docs + sample app (todo: link demo)

Related tickets / pointers:
- see JIRA-4521 (route-level presets)
- runtime PR 1839: early cancel telemetry support (infra-side)
- slack thread: #sdk-cost-shrink (discussion re: conservative presets)

Notes to self / TODO for next pass:
- formalize small entropy-based threshold formula for the edge 8-token probe.
- design a tiny on-device predictor sketch (sketch a tiny transformer or even a bag-of-ngrams logistic reg) and run a tabletop test on historical prompts.
- mock cost-sim using historical traffic sample (pick 10k prompts, simulate heuristics).

Random brain-dump heuristics (quick):
- prefer lowering max_new_tokens before lowering temperature for tasks that are extraction-focused.
- for code-gen: prefer deterministic (low temp) but allow a short sampled "variations" endpoint for optional expansions.
- for multi-turn chat: prioritize prefix caching (previous assistant messages) over whole context to reduce tokens.

End of scratchbook.
summary: Personal scratch notes on client-side cost/fidelity levers, heuristics, experiment ideas, telemetry and simple ASCII flows.
